title: Privileges in a token
description:
Read a token's privilege list and check what a program may do.

```
SeShutdownPrivilege        disabled
SeChangeNotifyPrivilege    enabled (by default)
SeDebugPrivilege           not present
need SeShutdownPrivilege -> present but disabled: enable it first (AdjustTokenPrivileges)
```
hints: `attributes & SE_PRIVILEGE_ENABLED` tells whether it is on now (lesson 7.05).
A privilege can only be enabled if the token already has it; elevation (running as administrator) is what adds more.
requirements: Privileges are a name and attribute flags (`SE_PRIVILEGE_ENABLED` 0x2, `ENABLED_BY_DEFAULT` 0x1).
`check(name)` says not present, present but disabled, or enabled.
Enabling a privilege that is not present fails, as it does in Windows.
stretch: List your own process's privileges with `GetTokenInformation(TokenPrivileges)`.
